name.en-US: Light at the End of the Tunnel

reviewContent.en-US:
I’ve seen Hadestown a bunch of times, and every time I’m blown away, but this cast was something else! Maia Reficco as Eurydice and Jordan Fisher as Orpheus were incredible. Jordan’s take on Orpheus was so different from the original—he felt more aware, passionate, and emotional. It really made his journey hit harder, and his chemistry with Maia was just perfect.

Even though I’ve seen this show so many times, there are still new things to notice. This time, I was really struck by the direction during Chant. The way everything came together—voices, movement, the lighting—it was just mind-blowing.

Honestly, this was my favorite production so far. Hadestown keeps finding ways to surprise me, and I love it more every time.

I went into Happy Ending not knowing what to expect—I’d only heard the set was amazing. Turns out, that’s an understatement! This show ended up being my favorite of the year.

First of all, seeing Darren Criss live as Oliver and Helen J. Shen as Claire was such a treat. Darren’s portrayal of a forgotten robot was surprisingly moving—it’s a performance I won’t forget anytime soon. Helen brought so much heart and depth to Claire, making their connection feel so real.

The set is everything people said it would be and more. The way it uses lighting and projections to show memories is just beautiful, especially since the story leans so heavily into themes of friendship, romance, memory, and mortality. The design really ties it all together in such a creative and emotional way.

This musical hits all the right notes—it’s funny, heartwarming, heartbreaking, and adorable, all at once. It’s a tear-jerker, for sure, but also leaves you with so much to think about.
